_comment: The onboarding question taxonomy. Topics, not questions.
This file contains NO ANSWERS and must never contain any. It is the shared
half of the north star's line: that a Greenhouse form asks about visa
sponsorship is public knowledge every account benefits from, while what any
person said is theirs alone and lives in their own store. That property is
what lets this file ship in the repository and survive an open-source
publish. A proposal to put answer values here breaks it.
Derived from 100 real employer questions observed across Greenhouse, Ashby,
Lever, Workday, SmartRecruiters and Oracle. Those 100 collapse to the topics
below because employers ask the same thing many ways: sponsorship appeared
six times, relocation five, political contributions four, sexual orientation
four. Asking a person thirty topics instead of a hundred questions is the
difference between twenty minutes and giving up.
`match` is how an unseen phrasing is recognised as a topic already answered.
Every term must appear in the question text, lowercased. scripts/
questionnaire.py checks this taxonomy against a real answer store and fails
when an observed question matches no topic, so the file cannot silently fall
behind what employers actually ask.
tier 1  blocking. No application completes without it.
tier 2  high frequency, asked during onboarding.
tier 3  long tail, captured on first encounter in Needs you.
`perIdentity` marks topics whose answer differs by the posting's country.
A person with a US and an India right to work has two of each of these, and
one profile row per user cannot hold them.

topics.ask: Which countries can you work in without needing sponsorship?
topics.why: Blocks almost every application, and asked in nearly every jurisdiction's phrasing.

topics.ask: Which countries would you need visa sponsorship for, now or in future?
topics.why: Six distinct phrasings observed. Always paired with work authorisation and always required.

topics.ask: Are you willing to relocate for the right role?
topics.why: Five phrasings observed. Cheap to answer, blocks applications when missing.

topics.ask: Which work setups will you take?
topics.why: Drives both form answers and search gating.

topics.ask: What notice do you have to give, and when could you start?
topics.why: Required on most non-US forms and on every Indian one.

topics.ask: What phone number should applications use?
topics.why: Identity field. No form completes without it.

topics.ask: What postal address should applications use?
topics.why: Per identity: a US application and an India application need different addresses, and choosing the wrong one is a real defect this project already fixed once.

topics.ask: How many years of professional experience do you have?
topics.why: Asked as a bare number and as per-skill variants. Also feeds the experience gate.

topics.ask: What is your highest degree, and from which school and field of study?
topics.why: Three required dropdowns on every Greenhouse education block, and the answer never changes. One of them parked a real application.

topics.ask: Which profile links should applications include?
topics.why: Nearly universal and trivially answered once.

topics.ask: What full name should be typed as your electronic signature?
topics.why: A submit-blocking field on legal-declaration forms.

topics.ask: What compensation are you looking for?
topics.why: Blocks Indian and screening-heavy US forms. Sensitive: stored only with explicit per-field consent, never rendered into board HTML.

topics.ask: What are you currently paid?
topics.why: Illegal to ask in several US states and routine in India. Sensitive, and a person may decline.

topics.ask: If a posting states a range you find acceptable, may Jobby acknowledge it on your behalf?
match: acknowledge and agree that this range
topics.why: A policy rather than a fact: the answer depends on the posted range, so it is a standing rule with a floor.

topics.ask: Are you willing to complete a background check if an offer is made?
topics.why: Willingness, which is a different question from authorising one now. Kept distinct on purpose.

topics.ask: May interviews be recorded and transcribed?
topics.why: Consent, so it must be the person's own choice and never a default.

topics.ask: Are you bound by any non-compete, non-solicit or other restrictive covenant?
topics.why: Four phrasings observed. A legal declaration, so a wrong answer matters more than a missing one.

topics.ask: Do you have any conflicts of interest to disclose?
topics.why: Five phrasings, and the honest answer is usually the same across all of them.

topics.ask: Are you, or is a close relative, a current or former government official?
topics.why: Anti-bribery declaration, common in finance and public-sector postings.

topics.ask: Have you made political contributions in the last two years?
topics.why: Four phrasings, near-universal in US financial-services forms.

topics.ask: Have you ever been debarred or suspended from federal contracting?
topics.why: Required wherever federal contracts are involved.

topics.ask: Have you worked at, or consulted for, the company you are applying to, and do you know anyone who works there?
topics.why: Asked by name on the employer's own form. The prior-employment half has a standing answer; who you know there still depends on the employer.

topics.ask: Will you accept the in-office schedule a posting states, whatever it is?
match: days per week in the office
topics.why: Distinct from work-setup, which is a preference. This one is the employer's stated arrangement asked as an acceptance, and it blocks submission when it goes unanswered.

topics.ask: Can you provide documentation of the employment and education on your resume?
match: verify the information on your resume
topics.why: A required screening field on Greenhouse forms and answerable once. Not the same as authorising a background check, which stays separate.

topics.ask: How should Jobby answer 'how did you hear about this job'?
topics.why: A standing rule, not a fact. The honest answer is the same every time.

topics.ask: May employers retain your details and contact you about future roles?
topics.why: Consent, and it is asked often enough to be worth settling once.

topics.ask: Jobby will tick truth attestations only when nothing in the application was inferred. Confirm you want that.
topics.why: A safety rule surfaced as a choice, because it is the user's signature being given. Never a silent default.

topics.ask: Employers often ask optional demographic questions. What should Jobby do?
topics.why: Ten observed phrasings across gender, ethnicity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, age and date of birth. Nearly always optional on the form, so declining is a complete answer. Presented once as a single consented choice rather than as ten questions, and stored per field. Never rendered into board HTML.

topics.ask: Rate yourself on a named tool, one to ten.
topics.why: The tool named varies by posting, so it cannot be pre-answered. Parks in Needs you.

topics.ask: What are you looking for in your next role, and what do you want to avoid?
match: looking for in your next role
topics.why: Genuine free text, and one of only a handful. Answered once in the person's own words and replayed, never regenerated.

topics.ask: Describe yourself in a short phrase.
topics.why: Short free text reused across forms.

topics.ask: How has AI changed how you work, and do you have a personal AI project?
match: personal project or side experiment in ai
ai changed the way you approach
topics.why: Currently common in this person's target market and may not generalise. Tier 3 until a second user's corpus says otherwise.

topics.ask: What is the highest years-of-experience requirement you would still apply to?
topics.why: A search preference rather than a form answer. Belongs with search config, recorded here so it is not asked twice.

_comment: Not a questionnaire. Twelve narrative entries in the source corpus, each a
worked example a free-text answer draws from. A stranger arrives with none
of these and no amount of resume parsing produces one, which is why this is
an interview rather than a form and is the real elicitation problem.
Prompts below are the themes observed, generalised away from one person's
specifics. Ask for two or three at signup, not twelve.
prompts: A time you delivered under an impossible constraint.
A time you drove adoption or influence without authority.
A time you were right against consensus, and how you proved it.
The thing you have built that you are proudest of, and what broke.
A time you earned trust at scale, with many stakeholders.
A time you took ownership of something ambiguous and unowned.
A time customer obsession cost you something.
A time frugality or initiative produced a result budget would not have.

_comment: Entries in a stored answer file that are NOT employer questions and are
therefore not the taxonomy's job to cover. Listed rather than silently
skipped, because an uncounted exclusion is how a real gap hides.
These are Jobby's own operating rules that were saved without a policy tag.
They belong with the standing policies, and the honest fix is upstream in
the store rather than a special case here.

match: tailored resume or cover letter be rebuilt
rules.why: An internal regeneration rule. No employer asks it.
Jobby's own handling policy for OTP, verification links and ATS account creation. An operating rule, and one the refusal boundaries already cover.
